result.summary: This PR adds three hardening checks to the read-only BDB parser (BerkeleyRODatabase::Open in migrate.cpp): rejecting btree pages visited more than once via different parent paths, rejecting overflow pages revisited in an empty-data cycle, and bounding total record size per page to the page size. Each fix is a separate commit with a hand-crafted regression test in db_tests.cpp, and the new error strings are added to the fuzz allow-list.
result.problem: A user who runs migratewallet, loads a legacy .dat wallet, or runs bitcoin-wallet feeds an attacker-supplied or corrupted BDB file to this parser. Three crafted-file cases bypass the level-consistency check added in #34959 and can turn a small file (as little as 8KB or 256KB) into exponential parsing work or an OOM (54MB to ~800MB observed), a CPU/memory exhaustion DoS.

result.card: This PR adds three hardening checks to the read-only BDB parser (migrate.cpp) used by migratewallet, legacy wallet loading, and bitcoin-wallet: rejecting btree pages revisited via a different parent path, rejecting overflow pages that cycle through empty pages, and bounding a page's total record size to the page size. It closes DoS gaps left after #34959, with concrete evidence: an ~8KB crafted file with shared subtrees never finishes, and a 256KB file drives RSS from 54MB to ~800MB. Each fix has its own commit and a hand-crafted regression test in db_tests.cpp, and it supersedes #35992 which proposed only the third fix alone. No reviewer has yet commented (Crickets), but the code appears ready for review with clear per-case tests. No fund-safety risk; all fixes are additive rejections that do not change parsing of valid files.
